blocks.content: Two containers on the same Docker network can talk to each other directly, no host port mapping required at all, exactly the mechanism a typical app-plus-database setup relies on.

Any two containers attached to the same Docker network can reach each other over that network directly, an app container can open a connection straight to a database container's internal port, entirely bypassing the host.

blocks.alt: Direct communication, entirely within the Docker network

blocks.content: 2. Addressed by Name, Not Just IP
blocks.text: 2. Addressed by Name, Not Just IP

blocks.content: On a custom network specifically, this communication happens by container name, an application configured to connect to a host called db on port 5432 just works, Docker's embedded DNS resolves db to that container's actual internal IP automatically.

blocks.alt: A name in application config, resolved automatically

blocks.content:
# Inside the app container's connection string
postgresql://db:5432/myapp
# "db" resolves automatically to the database container's IP

blocks.content: 3. Different Networks Cannot Reach Each Other
blocks.text: 3. Different Networks Cannot Reach Each Other

blocks.content: This same-network requirement is a real boundary, containers on entirely separate Docker networks cannot reach each other at all by default, exactly the isolation behavior covered in the Custom Networks topic, useful for keeping unrelated stacks genuinely apart on the same host.

blocks.alt: Separate networks are genuinely isolated from each other

blocks.content: When two otherwise-isolated groups of containers do need to talk, the fix is attaching one specific container to both networks, that container can then see (and be reached from) both sides, without opening up either network wholesale.

blocks.alt: One container, deliberately bridging two otherwise-separate networks

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Containers on the same Docker network reach each other directly, and on a custom network, by name, without any host port mapping involved.
Containers on different networks cannot reach each other by default, a real isolation boundary, not just a convention.
